//test: `npm run typecheck` is IN this chain, and must stay in it. vitest strips types
without checking them, so before 2026-08-30 a plant the compiler catches read as
"no test noticed": deleting the `rasterRef` key from the SectionMeta interface left
`vitest run` at 6041 passed with zero red rows while `npx tsc --noEmit` reported 23
errors. Every "merged tree green" claim in the review packets and the lane log quotes
`npm test`, and the SectionMeta ref set — an erasure-critical site — is guarded ONLY
by tsc. A separate `check` script would have left that gap open for anyone who types
`npm test`, which is everyone.
ORDER: typecheck runs BEFORE vitest, so a type error stops the chain without paying
for the suite. Do not read that as 'fails in tsc's time' — the four check:* scripts
and check-harness-guards run FIRST and are part of the wait. Measured on one machine
2026-08-30, overseer's re-run of the merged tree: check:* chain 4.6s, `npm run
typecheck` 4.5s, whole green `npm test` 19.9s; the planted type error came back rc=2
at 13.6s with vitest never invoked (zero `Test Files` lines). So the saving is roughly
the suite, not the whole run, and the split is what to re-derive if these drift — time
the pieces, do not attribute the stop to tsc alone. Code that does not typecheck makes
the suite's verdict meaningless anyway. The queue row
that booked this assumed tsc was SLOWER than the suite and would need its own script;
it is under half, so the naive add is also the correct one.
It composes `npm run typecheck` rather than spelling `tsc --noEmit` a second time, so
there is one definition of how this repo typechecks.
`check-python-resolver.mjs` is in this chain because vitest CANNOT execute the Python
half of the peer-path resolver, `scratchpad/lib/suite_paths.py`, which six instruments
import and which had no test file in any language at any path until 2026-09-02. A test
nothing runs is the empty population that whole parcel exists to end, so the rows run
here, where everything else in this repo runs. It needs no Python package: the rows are
stdlib `unittest`, and `python3` is already required by check-ledger-timestamps in this
same chain.
scripts.test: node scripts/check-test-collection.mjs && node scripts/check-pseudo-skip.mjs && node scripts/check-peer-path-literals.mjs && node scripts/check-object-stringify.mjs && node scripts/check-ledger-timestamps.mjs && node scripts/check-python-resolver.mjs && node scratchpad/check-harness-guards.mjs && npm run typecheck && vitest run

//overrides: electron-vite@5 (the newest stable) declares a peer of vite@^5 || ^6 || ^7, so a plain
`npm install` or `npm ci` on this repo dies with ERESOLVE against our vite@8.
This override asserts a narrow, empirical claim: THIS combination — vite 8 +
electron-vite 5 + @vitejs/plugin-react 6 — is the tree we already run. It is what
`npm run dev`, `npm run build`, `npm run preview` and `npm test` all use today, and it
passes the full vitest suite. It is NOT a claim that electron-vite 5 is compatible with
vite 8 in general; only that nothing Aurora exercises is broken by the gap.
REMOVAL CONDITION: electron-vite 6 (currently 6.0.0-beta.1) widens the peer to include
^8.0.0. When electron-vite@6 ships stable, bump the dependency and DELETE this override
and this note. Recheck with: npm view electron-vite dist-tags
